card.title: The paper found after Bayes died

panels.text: Thomas Bayes, an 18th-century minister and mathematician, studied how to use evidence to put limits on an unknown quantity.
After his death, his family passed his papers to a friend, Richard Price. Price edited the manuscript for two years.
It was read aloud at the Royal Society on 23 December 1763 and published that year as An Essay Towards Solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances.

Independently, Pierre-Simon Laplace worked out the same idea: take a prior probability, add evidence, and get an updated one. Today it is Bayes' theorem, a rule for updating your belief when new information arrives.

probes.question: In Bayesian updating, what is the prior probability?
options: The probability after seeing the evidence
The chance the evidence is wrong
The estimate before the new evidence is observed

probes.question: True or false: Bayes' theorem is widely invoked to justify how someone should update beliefs after new information.
